title: Measure Feeding During Large Population Swarming with Bioluminescent Bacteria
author: Serena Ding
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.53kg8kw
materials: Initialise the IVIS system via the Living Image software.

Set up imaging parameters within the Living Image software interface. Set stage temperature to 20 °C , designate auto-saving directory for acquired images, and set up acquisition sequence parameters. Bioluminescence acquisition parameters: subject height: 0.5 cm; field of view: C; expososure: 1 second; frame interval: 1 minute (for N2 worms) and 2 minutes (for DA609 worms); excitation: block; emission: open; luminescence binning: 4; photograph binning: 4; luminescence F/stop: 1; photograph F/stop: 1; batch sequence: true; sequence 1 length: 99; sequence 2 length: 35. These imaging parameters have been determined in advance for the experiment and are saved as a .xsq configuration file, which can be loaded into the imaging software.

steps.title: Prepare Bacterial Stock (Day -2)
steps.instruction: Streak bioluminescent bacteria frozen stock onto an LB plate containing 50 μg/mL ampicillin and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

substeps.instruction: Note: A streaked plate can be re-used within 1 month if single colonies are available; otherwise, re-streak onto a new LB/ampicillin plate.

steps.title: Prepare Bacterial Culture (Day -1)
steps.instruction: At approximately 5pm, prepare a bacterial culture in a 300 mL volumetric flask.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 mL LB broth and 100 μL ampicillin stock solution (50mg/mL).
Inoculate with a single colony of bioluminescent bacteria from the streaked plate.
Incubate at 37 °C shaking at 220 rpm overnight.

steps.title: Prepare Bacteria for Seeding (Day 0)
steps.instruction: At approximately 10am, remove the overnight culture from the shaking incubator and leave it at room temperature on the bench until use.

substeps.instruction: Do not store the culture at 4 °C as this will abolish the signal; grow a fresh overnight culture for each day of experiment.

steps.title: Prepare Imaging Plates
steps.instruction: Warm imaging plates to room temperature and seed with bacteria.

substeps.instruction: Remove two 90mm plates (containing 35 mL low peptone agar) and two 35mm plates (containing 3.5 mL low peptone agar) from the 4 °C cold room and incubate at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Seed 500 μL of bacteria culture onto the center of each 90mm plate and 20 μL onto the center of each 35mm plate.
Dry the plates in a laminar flow hood (setting II) for 2 hours (90mm) and 30 minutes (35mm) respectively.

steps.title: Prepare Bacterial Culture for Use
steps.instruction: Prepare the remaining overnight culture for recording and seeding.

substeps.instruction: Swirl the flask to resuspend bacteria cells that may have settled.
Measure the optical density of the bacteria culture using a spectrophotometer for the record.

steps.title: Synchronize and Harvest Worms
steps.instruction: Prepare synchronized adult worms for the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Bleach synchronize animals from three 90mm plates (ensuring presence of gravid hermaphrodites) and leave on a rotator at 20 °C until use.
Re-feed worms onto three pre-seeded 90mm plates using a glass pipette and incubate at 20 °C, monitoring to ensure food is available.
Harvest synchronized adult worms using M9 buffer and transfer them into a 15 mL Falcon tube, pooling from three large plates.

steps.title: Wash and Concentrate Worms
steps.instruction: Wash the worms to remove contaminating bacteria.

substeps.instruction: Wash worms twice with M9 buffer by topping up the tube with M9.
Spin at 1500 rpm/210 rcf (ascending 9, descending 7) and aspire the supernatant, leaving the loose pellet intact.
After the final wash, leave the loose worm pellet.

steps.title: Set Up Imaging Samples
steps.instruction: Transfer worms to the imaging plates and prepare for IVIS imaging.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve imaging plates from the flow hood; select and label one 90mm and one 35mm plate for the experiment.
Remove as much supernatant as possible from the 15 mL Falcon tube.
Using a glass pipette with a medicine dropper bulb, transfer all worms to the 90mm imaging plate, keeping the droplet small to avoid spilling onto the bacterial lawn.
Place the 15 mL Falcon tube containing the worm pellet in a styrofoam box and transport to the IVIS imaging system.

steps.title: Acquire Bioluminescence Images
steps.instruction: Perform imaging using the IVIS system.

substeps.instruction: Place the 90mm imaging sample and the no-worm 35mm control plate inside the IVIS chamber within the laser grid guidelines.
Close the chamber door and start acquisition via the software immediately (do not wait for liquid to be absorbed into the media).

steps.title: Analyze Imaging Data
steps.instruction: Quantify the bioluminescent signal using software.

substeps.instruction: Use Living Image software to read the signal across the acquisition sequence by measuring radiance (photons/s) for a defined region of interest.
Export the signal as a tab-delimited text file for downstream analysis.
